report.source_text: Diagnostic paracentesis was performed with the resulting fluid biochemistry as follows: lactate dehydrogenase of 1255 U/L, total protein of 53 g/L, pH 7.76 and alkaline phosphatase of 51 U/L. Fluid cytology showed neoplastic cells with moderate amount of eosinophilic cytoplasm and rare papillary-like structures. Immunochemistry staining showed PAX8-positive, CD10-positive and CK7-positive cells consistent with carcinoma of renal origin (figure 3). There was no bacterial growth from the ascitic fluid culture.

report.source_text: He was subsequently reviewed by the Medical Oncology team, which commenced on 20 mg daily dose of cabozantinib, a small-molecule tyrosine kinase inhibitor. He initially reported good improvement in his abdominal pain symptoms within 1 month of therapy commencement. This improvement was further supported by a repeat staging CT of the brain, chest, abdomen and pelvis, showing stable peritoneal and pulmonary nodules and resolution of ascites and pleural effusion. There was no evidence of other metastatic foci on CT and whole-body bone scan.

clinician.final_diagnosis: pT2 Nx type 1 papillary renal cell carcinoma (pRCC)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 69-year-old man underwent laparoscopic left radical nephrectomy for an 80 mm Bosniak IV cystic renal mass. Histopathology revealed pT2 Nx type 1 papillary RCC, nuclear grade 2, with negative surgical margins, tumor confined within the renal capsule, no lymphovascular invasion, and necrotic features present. Five months post-nephrectomy, he presented with worsening generalized abdominal pain, abdominal distension, and loss of appetite. Physical examination revealed ascites with mild abdominal tenderness; he was haemodynamically stable with no peritonism or systemic infection signs. CT imaging identified moderate-volume ascites with peritoneal nodules, right pleural effusion, and a 14 mm right apical subpleural nodule, with no locoregional recurrence in the left renal bed. Diagnostic paracentesis revealed ascitic fluid with elevated LDH (1255 U/L), total protein 53 g/L, and cytology showing neoplastic cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and rare papillary-like structures. Immunochemistry staining was PAX8-positive, CD10-positive, and CK7-positive, consistent with carcinoma of renal origin. These findings confirmed metastatic papillary RCC with peritoneal involvement. He was commenced on cabozantinib 20 mg daily by Medical Oncology, with good symptomatic improvement within 1 month and imaging evidence of stable peritoneal and pulmonary nodules with resolution of ascites and pleural effusion.
